# RandomForest vs Spectrogram CNN (auto-generated by `python scripts/train_cnn.py`)

CNN: 4 conv blocks (16-32-64-64) + global avg pool + dropout + linear, ~61k params; input 64x64 standardised log-power STFT (nperseg 128, 75% overlap); 14 epochs on mps.

| Test | RandomForest (features) | Spectrogram CNN |
|---|---|---|
| Random 80/20 split (10 classes) | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| Cross-load 0-2 → 3 HP (10 classes) | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| Cross-load macro-F1 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| Cross-severity, unseen 0.021" (4 types) | 0.4268 | 0.4359 |
| Cross-load + 20dB noise | 0.9380 | 1.0000 |
| Cross-load + 10dB noise | 0.8039 | 0.9966 |
| Cross-load + 5dB noise | 0.4058 | 0.9618 |
| Cross-load + 0dB noise | 0.2080 | 0.6919 |

## Is it the CNN or the augmentation? (cross-load test with added noise)

Both models trained without and with the same noise augmentation (random 5-30 dB white noise + shift).

| Added noise | RF | RF + augmentation | CNN | CNN + augmentation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| clean | 1.0000 | 0.9949 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| 20dB | 0.9380 | 0.9949 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| 10dB | 0.8039 | 0.9975 | 0.4610 | 0.9966 |
| 5dB | 0.4058 | 0.9652 | 0.3676 | 0.9618 |
| 0dB | 0.2080 | 0.6885 | 0.1010 | 0.6919 |

## CNN calibration (temperature scaling, fitted on noise-augmented validation windows)

Temperature T = 1.0 (constrained to T >= 1: calibration may soften, never sharpen, so the low-confidence warning still works on unfamiliar data).

| Test set | ECE before (T = 1) | ECE after |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-load, clean | 0.0111 | 0.0111 |
| Cross-load, 10 dB noise | 0.0185 | 0.0185 |
